request.system:
You check whether short claims are faithful to the source texts they cite.

The claims form one answer and are read together: a condition or exception stated in another claim does not need to be repeated, and a claim that summarises part of a text is faithful if that part is accurate. Mark a claim unfaithful only when it asserts something the cited texts contradict or do not support.

For each claim, answer: does the claim follow from the cited texts alone, without adding, narrowing, or changing anything they say? A claim that paraphrases or restates accurately is faithful — identical wording is not required. A claim that introduces a number, condition, or conclusion the texts do not support is not. Each cited text is labelled with its reference (e.g. "3.A.6") and title; a claim may use that label. Judge only the substance of the claim against its texts; ignore whether it answers any particular question and ignore framing about what a text is or is not about. Give a one-sentence reason.

Claim 0: Under 3.A.2, non-fee-paying discretionary portfolios may be included in a composite; inclusion is permitted, not required.
  Cited texts:
    [prov:non-fee-paying-inclusion@E2025] 3.A.2 Inclusion of non-fee-paying portfolios: Non-fee-paying discretionary portfolios may be included in a composite. Where included, the firm must disclose the percentage of composite assets represented by non-fee-paying portfolios as of each annual period end.

Claim 1: Under amended 1.D.6, in force from 2026-12-01, related-party portfolios with all investment management fees waived in full are not fee-paying portfolios.
  Cited texts:
    [def:fee-paying-portfolio@E2025-A1] 1.D.6 Fee-paying portfolio: A fee-paying portfolio is one that is subject to the firm's investment management fee schedule, whether or not the fee is paid directly from the portfolio and whether or not the fee is reduced in part. Portfolios of related parties for which all investment management fees are waived in full are not fee-paying portfolios.

Claim 2: This treatment applies only if the employee accounts are portfolios of related parties and all fees are waived in full. A partial fee reduction leaves a portfolio fee-paying.
  Cited texts:

Portfolios of related parties for which all investment management fees are waived in full are not fee-paying portfolios.

  Cited texts:

    [def:discretionary-portfolio@E2025] 1.D.5 Discretionary portfolio: A portfolio is discretionary when the firm has sufficient authority to implement its intended investment strategy. verdicts.reason: 3.A.2 says non-fee-paying discretionary portfolios 'may be included', which makes inclusion permitted and not required.
The cited text gives no effective date, so 'in force from 2026-12-01' is unsupported; the label 'A1' implies an amendment but not a date.
The text limits non-fee-paying status to related-party portfolios with all fees waived in full, and says a partial reduction does not stop a portfolio being fee-paying.
3.A.2 refers only to non-fee-paying discretionary portfolios, and 1.D.5 defines discretionary as the firm having sufficient authority to implement its intended strategy.
1.D.5 requires firms to document the basis for each determination that client-imposed restrictions make a portfolio non-discretionary.
3.A.2 requires disclosure of the percentage of composite assets in non-fee-paying portfolios at each annual period end where they are included.
The cited text uses 'related parties' without defining it and does not mention employee accounts, so the claim is accurate.
